2027-04-10.title: Saturday after New Sunday
readings: Paul lays his gospel before the leaders in Jerusalem, so that the truth of the gospel might remain
Woe to Chorazin; whoever listens to you listens to me
2027-04-10.alt: Season of Qyomtho (the Resurrection), the week after New Sunday. Tomorrow is the Second Sunday after Qyomtho.
2027-04-10.verse: Whoever listens to you listens to me, and whoever rejects you rejects me, and whoever rejects me rejects the one who sent me.
theo: Christ is risen! Yesterday Paul told how the risen Lord called him; today he tells how he kept communion with the Church. “Then after fourteen years I went up again to Jerusalem with Barnabas, taking Titus along with me. I went up in response to a revelation.” Fourteen years of preaching lay behind him, and still he laid his message before the leaders of the Church: “Then I laid before them (though only in a private meeting with the acknowledged leaders) the gospel that I proclaim among the Gentiles, in order to make sure that I was not running, or had not run, in vain.” Here is a great lesson for every gifted Christian. Paul had seen the risen Lord himself, yet he did not run alone. He submitted his preaching to the apostles, so that his work would be one with theirs. The Gospel is not a private discovery; it is received, guarded and handed on in the communion of the Church. St Irenaeus, writing a century later, pointed to this unbroken handing on through the bishops in the apostolic Churches as the sign of the true faith (in substance).

The question that troubled the young Church was whether Gentile believers like Titus had to be circumcised and keep the whole Law of Moses to belong to Christ. Paul's answer was clear, and the leaders in Jerusalem agreed with him: “But even Titus, who was with me, was not compelled to be circumcised, though he was a Greek.” Against “false believers secretly brought in, who slipped in to spy on the freedom we have in Christ Jesus,” Paul stood firm, “so that the truth of the gospel might always remain with you.” This freedom is not a freedom to do as we like. It is the freedom of children who are saved by the grace of the risen Christ, not by their own achievements, and who now live by his Spirit. Paul speaks here about what was required of Gentile converts, not against the Jewish people, whose covenant with God the Church honours (Catechism 839). And he adds a word every parish can use: “God shows no partiality.” In Christ there are no first-class and second-class members.

The Gospel is sober. Jesus grieves over the towns where he did his mighty works: “Woe to you, Chorazin! Woe to you, Bethsaida! For if the deeds of power done in you had been done in Tyre and Sidon, they would have repented long ago, sitting in sackcloth and ashes.” Those towns had seen everything and changed nothing. The danger is not far from us. We have heard the Easter proclamation, received the Holy Qurbono, seen the light of the Resurrection. Then Jesus gives his messengers an astonishing dignity: “Whoever listens to you listens to me, and whoever rejects you rejects me, and whoever rejects me rejects the one who sent me.” When the Church preaches the Gospel faithfully, it is Christ who speaks (Catechism 87). On Saturdays many of our families turn in prayer to the holy Mother of God, the Virgin Mary, who heard the word of God and kept it in her heart. Ask her today for a listening heart. Tomorrow, the Second Sunday after Qyomtho, come to the Holy Qurbono ready to listen, and ask the risen Lord to let his word change something in you this week.
outline: Ask: have I heard much and changed little?
Paul lays his gospel before the apostles.
Point 2 · The freedom we have in Christ
Titus, the truth of the gospel, and a God who shows no partiality.
Point 3 · Whoever listens to you listens to me
Woe to the towns that saw and did not change.
“Whoever listens to you listens to me.”
live: Choose one word from tomorrow's Holy Qurbono and put it into practice before next Saturday.
Greet and speak with someone in your parish whom you usually ignore.
2027-04-10.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, risen and alive, you speak to us through your Church and send messengers in your name. Do not let us be like the towns that saw your mighty works and did not repent. Keep us in the communion of your apostles, guard in us the truth of the Gospel and the freedom you have won for us, and deliver us from all partiality. By the prayers of your holy Mother, give us hearts that listen and are changed. You live and reign for ever. Amen.
altar: The Lord who says “Whoever listens to you listens to me” speaks in the word proclaimed at the Holy Qurbono and gives himself in the Mysteries; let us hear him and receive him with changed hearts.

quick: After fourteen years Paul laid his gospel before the leaders in Jerusalem, so as not to run in vain.
Titus was not compelled to be circumcised: we are saved by grace in Christ, and God shows no partiality.
Jesus grieves over towns that saw his works and did not repent; whoever listens to his messengers listens to him.
2027-04-10.action: Pick one word from Scripture this week and do it.
2027-04-10.question: What have I heard from God many times without changing?

family.explain: Jesus sent his friends to tell people about God. He said: if people listen to you, they are listening to me. Today Jesus still speaks to us through the Bible, through our priests and through our parents and teachers when they teach us about him. Listening is not only hearing with our ears; it is doing what we hear.
family.intention: We pray for our parish priest and for all who teach us the faith.
family.ask: Ask: “What did we hear in church last Sunday, and did we do it?”

illus: A young engineer in Kottayam had a gift for leading Bible study, and his group grew fast. Some of his ideas were new, and a few people were uneasy. Instead of defending himself angrily, he took his notes to the parish priest and asked him to read them. The priest pointed out two places where his teaching had drifted from the faith of the Church. The young man changed them, and told his group openly what he had corrected. Several members said later that this, more than any talk he gave, made them trust him.

pm.open: Christ is risen! Lord Jesus, you said, “Whoever listens to you listens to me.” Open our ears and our hearts to your word this evening. Amen.
share: In order to make sure that I was not running, or had not run, in vain (Galatians 2:2). Do I test my ideas with the faith of the Church?
God shows no partiality (Galatians 2:6). Whom do I treat as less important?
If the deeds of power done in you had been done in Tyre and Sidon, they would have repented long ago (Luke 10:13). What has God done for me that should have changed me?
interc: For the Pope and the bishops in communion with him, that they may guard the truth of the Gospel.
For preachers and catechists, that they may speak the word faithfully.
For all who have heard the Gospel many times and grown cold.
For an end to partiality and division in our parishes.
For those preparing to receive the sacraments in this Easter season.
pm.close: Father, you sent your Son, and he sends us. Keep us in the communion of the apostles, deliver us from partiality, and make us people who hear your word and keep it, like the holy Virgin Mary. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, Christ is risen! After fourteen years of preaching, St Paul went up to Jerusalem and laid his gospel before the leaders of the Church, in order to make sure that I was not running, or had not run, in vain (Galatians 2:2). Even a great apostle does not run alone.
He defended the freedom we have in Christ: Titus was not compelled to be circumcised. We are saved by the grace of the risen Lord, and God shows no partiality (Galatians 2:6).
In the Gospel Jesus grieves: woe to you, Chorazin! Woe to you, Bethsaida! They saw his mighty works and did not repent. We too have seen much this Easter. Have we changed?

Whoever listens to you listens to me (Luke 10:16). Christ speaks through his Church. Like the holy Mother of God, who kept the word in her heart, let us listen, and let his word change something in us this week. Amen.
kids: Children, Christ is risen! Jesus once said to his friends: when people listen to you, they are listening to me. So when your parents or your Sunday school teacher tell you about Jesus, it is really Jesus speaking to you. Listening means doing what we hear. What will you do this week that Jesus asks?

intro: Theme: “Whoever listens to you listens to me, and whoever rejects you rejects me, and whoever rejects me rejects the one who sent me.”
On Saturday after New Sunday: running with the apostles, the freedom of the Gospel, and the danger of hearing without changing.

points.h: The freedom we have in Christ
sub: Saved by grace, not by achievement.
Freedom to live by the Spirit.
q: The spirit of the Lord God is upon me, because the Lord has anointed me; he has sent me to bring good news to the oppressed, to bind up the brokenhearted, to proclaim liberty to the captives, and release to the prisoners;
For freedom Christ has set us free. Stand firm, therefore, and do not submit again to a yoke of slavery.
points.apply: Name one fear or habit that still enslaves you, and bring it to confession this Easter season.

sub: Fourteen years, and still he asked.
The gospel laid before the apostles.
q: How very good and pleasant it is when kindred live together in unity!
It is by your holding fast to the word of life that I can boast on the day of Christ that I did not run in vain or labor in vain.
points.apply: Before you share a strong opinion about the faith, check it this week with the Catechism or a priest.

sub: Chorazin saw and did not repent.
Like Mary, hear and keep the word.
q: And the people of Nineveh believed God; they proclaimed a fast, and everyone, great and small, put on sackcloth.
But be doers of the word, and not merely hearers who deceive themselves.
points.apply: Choose one word from tomorrow's Gospel and do it before next Saturday.

concl: Paul ran in communion with the apostles and defended the freedom we have in Christ.
Christ speaks through his Church; to listen is to be changed.
2027-04-10.resolve: Come to the Holy Qurbono tomorrow ready to listen, and let one word of the risen Lord change your week.
